newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile investment to counter effects of bad weather.
newsitem.headline: Chile investment to counter effects of bad weather.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei announced on Monday night an 80 billion peso (165 million dollars) investment to deal with the effects of heavy rains that hit the country last week, leaving about 80,000 people homeless.
"The top priority in this winter plan is housing for the families that suffered most with the bad weather, and whose dificulties I know personally", Frei said.
The funds will be come from the budget of the ministries involved in the recovery plan, so the government will not require congressional approval for additional funding.
Heavy rains last week in Chile put an end to a year-long drought but at the same time severely damaged roads and crops and flooded houses along 9,500 miles (15,000 km) of Chilean territory.
The winter plan includes funds to repair roads, paths, contention walls and irrigation projects in the northern semi- arid valleys.
The government also expects to repair schools and health centers as part of the recovery plan.
